newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil set to begin Caspian exploration programme.
newsitem.headline: Statoil set to begin Caspian exploration programme.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday Azerbaijan authorities had given the green light for a three-year exploration phase in the Shakh Deniz area of the Caspian Sea.
Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the area contained roughly 2.5 billion barrels of oil. A production sharing agreement for the region has already been ratified by the authorities.
"The work programme for Shakh Deniz came officially into effect on October 17," said Thor Ivar Pedersen, head of Statoil's Azerbaijan operations.
"We're due to have finished the obligatory exploration phase on October 16, 1999. Shakh Deniz is regarded as one of the most promising prospects in the Azeri sector of the Caspian."
The work programme involves two wells and will start with the shooting of 800 square kilometres of three-dimensional seismic, probably next spring, Statoil said.

Operator British Petroleum and Statoil each hold 25.5 percent interest in the area. Other partners are Azeri state oil company Socar, Russia's Lukoil, Elf of France and state Iranian group National Iranian Oil Co with 10 percent each and Turkey's TPAO with nine percent.
